item.title: Bombardier, U.K.’s BAE explore partnership for future combat aircraft programs
item.description: Canadian business jet maker Bombardier said on Wednesday it had signed a strategic agreement with BAE Systems to explore opportunities to develop industrial and technology capabilities for future ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Canadian business jet maker Bombardier said on Wednesday it had signed a strategic agreement with BAE Systems to explore opportunities to develop industrial and technology capabilities for future combat air programs. Under the memorandum of understanding, the companies will assess opportunities in research and development, systems integration, workforce and supply-chain development, industrialization and lifecycle support as Canada deepens its involvement in next-generation combat air initiatives. The agreement underscores Bombardier’s push to expand its defence aerospace business. CEO Éric Martel said earlier this year the company saw growing opportunities for its defence unit, which converts business jets into special-mission aircraft, as Canada and Europe boost military spending and seek to diversify away from U.S. defence firms amid geopolitical tensions. Bombardier’s agreement with BAE comes months after Canada joined the Global Combat Air Programme, or GCAP, as an observer. Britain, Italy and Japan launched GCAP in 2022 to develop a next-generation stealth fighter by 2035. The program is led by Britain’s BAE Systems, Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Italy’s Leonardo. The Financial Times reported last week that Airbus executives were set to meet BAE Systems counterparts to discuss the European planemaker’s potential participation in GCAP, citing people familiar with the matter. (Reporting by Nandan Mandayam and Aatreyee Dasgupta in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar)

item.title: Survey: 82% of Young Canadians Lack Financial Confidence in at Least One Aspect of the Homebuying Process
item.description: New research highlights the financial pressures facing Canadians and the challenges of saving for a home, particularly among younger Canadians with only 18% of those aged 18-34 who say they feel ...
item.dc:creator: Business Wire
item.content:encoded: This press release is provided by Business Wire and is published as received. TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- New research highlights the financial pressures facing Canadians and the challenges of saving for a home, particularly among younger Canadians with only 18% of those aged 18-34 who say they feel confident navigating all financial aspects of buying a home. That’s compared to 35% aged 35 to 54 and 50% aged 55 and older. The 2026 Zown Homeownership & Financial Confidence Survey issued by Zown, a full-service, AI-powered real estate brokerage, and conducted among members of the Angus Reid Forum, found that younger Canadians identified several areas of homebuying finances they feel least confident navigating, including: The findings also reveal that just 13% of Canadians who have never owned a home but haven’t ruled out homeownership, feel confident navigating all financial aspects of buying a home, compared with 46% of current homeowners. For prospective buyers in this group, the areas of least confidence include: Canadians Dip Into Long-Term Savings to Cover Expenses The survey also found that 40% of Canadians tapped into their long-term savings to cover expenses or unexpected costs over the past year. Among those who accessed their savings, 29% used the money for emergencies or unexpected expenses, 22% for groceries and everyday purchases, and 13% for regular housing costs, including rent or mortgage payments. “Housing affordability isn’t just about the price of a home. It’s also about whether Canadians can afford to become homeowners in the first place,” said Rishard Rameez, Founder and CEO of Zown. “There’s a disconnect between the dream of homeownership and the financial reality many Canadians face. We’re asking people to save tens of thousands of dollars for a down payment when they’re already drawing on their savings to cover everyday expenses. That’s a fundamental challenge we can’t afford to overlook.” Canadians Across the Country Are Drawing on Long-Term Savings From roughly one-third to nearly half of respondents in each region, Canadians report dipping into long-term savings to manage financial pressures: As Canadians face growing challenges in saving for a home, Zown is focused on helping aspiring buyers overcome financial barriers and navigate the path to homeownership. About Zown Founded in 2022, Zown is an AI-powered real estate platform and licensed brokerage on a mission to make homeownership more affordable and accessible. Combining a personal AI agent with licensed real estate professionals, Zown guides buyers from education and home search through offer negotiation and closing, while providing upfront cashback to eligible buyers to reduce upfront costs. Zown has helped over 1,000 homebuyers transact over $700 million in real estate and returned more than $8 million in cashback. For more information, visit www.zown.ca. Methodology These findings are from a survey conducted by Zown from October 14 to October 16, 2026, among a representative sample of 1,500 online adult Canadians who are members of the Angus Reid Forum. The survey was conducted in English and French. For comparison purposes only, a probability sample of this size would carry a margin of error of +/- 2.53 percentage points, 19 times out of 20. item.title: Global shares are mixed after U.S. stock rally, and oil prices gain more than 1%
item.description: U.S. futures edged higher. Oil prices rose more than 1 per cent after an attack on a major Saudi Arabia refinery by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Tuesday renewed supply concerns. In early European ...
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: HONG KONG — Tech stocks have surged this week ahead of Wednesday’s meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve with markets anticipating no change to the benchmark U.S. interest rate, at least not yet. The rapid-growth tech sector is fuelled by easy access to credit and hyperscalers like Microsoft and Alphabet will post quarterly earnings reports after the bell. Amazon and Intel release earnings Thursday. The tech rally continued before the opening bell Wednesday as futures for the Nasdaq, already up two per cent this week, rose 0.4 per cent. Futures for the S&P 500 edged up 0.1 per cent, while those for the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 144 points, or 0.3 per cent. The Fed is in a bind, however, with higher energy prices from the conflict in the Middle East intensifying inflation. Benchmark U.S. crude rose more than two per cent early Wednesday after an attack on a major Saudi Arabian refinery by Iran-backed Houthi rebels this week. Brent crude oil, the international standard, is also up almost two per cent to US$111.38 a barrel. Alphabet is up almost two per cent early and Microsoft is essentially flat. Memory chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 11.4 per cent to its highest level in two weeks after it reported a record-high operating profit of 83.3 trillion won ($62.8 billion) for the last quarter, up nearly sevenfold from a year earlier and beating market estimates. In other early trading, the cryptocurrency platform Robinhood is down sharply after its quarterly profit fell short of expectations. Stellantis rose six per cent after the automaker stood by its guidance for the year despite heavy costs related to its turnaround bid. In Europe, Germany’s DAX edged up less than 0.1 per cent to 25,598.39, while the CAC 40 in Paris declined 0.1 per cent to 7,876.05. Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.3 per cent to 10,656.49. In Asia, South Korea’s Kospi surged 6.6 per cent to close at 6,012.44. The Bank of Japan begins a two-day policy meeting on Thursday, with markets expecting its benchmark interest rate to be unchanged. Treasury yields are relatively steady before the U.S. Federal Reserve announces its decision on interest rates. The Fed last month hiked the fed funds rate for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing inflation, but the widespread expectation on Wall Street is that it will hold rates steady this time. The yield on the 10-year Treasury, an important indicator on inflation for the Fed, edged up 0.25 per cent to 5.0 per cent early Wednesday. The U.S. dollar slid to 157.92 Japanese yen from 157.95 yen. The euro was trading at $1.1128, up from $1.1126. Elaine Lai, The Associated Press

item.title: Bank of Canada expected to hike key rate for 1st time since 2023
item.description: The Bank of Canada is widely expected to move its benchmark interest rate this morning for the first time in nearly a year.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — The Bank of Canada is widely expected to move its benchmark interest rate this morning for the first time in nearly a year. Financial markets and a Reuters poll of economists are betting that the central bank will deliver a quarter-point hike to its policy rate, the first increase in the key lending rate since July 2023. The bank’s policy rate has stood at 2.25 per cent for nearly a year now, a level most economists see as giving the economy a bit of a boost. But even as a tariff dispute with the United States threatens economic growth, the Bank of Canada has signalled it’s increasingly worried about inflation stemming from war in the Middle East. Monetary policymakers have said they’d look past the initial inflationary surge tied to rising energy prices but would raise the policy rate if there were signs price pressures could spread beyond the gas pumps. Alongside the rate decision, the Bank of Canada will also release updated forecasts for inflation and economic growth. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 28, 2026. Craig Lord, The Canadian Press
